native_mcp_support.notes: UPGRADED from SDK-experimental-only. MCP is now a documented first-class tool type: the function-calling page carries a 'Remote MCP (Model Context Protocol)' section and the Interactions API reference defines a tool of type 'mcp_server' with url / headers / name / allowed_tools. Constraints, verbatim: 'Remote MCP only works with Streamable HTTP servers. SSE (Server-Sent Events) servers are not supported'; server name 'must be strictly lowercase and alphanumeric'; 'MCP server names should not include the - character. Use snake_case server names instead'. CRITICAL CAVEAT that keeps this at medium confidence: the Interactions API Limitations section states 'Remote MCP: Gemini 3 does not support remote MCP, this is coming soon', so the server-side path is live only through the Antigravity managed agent (preview, default model gemini-3.7-flash, announced 2026-07-07). For direct model calls, MCP is still client-side via the google-genai SDK, where 'Built-in MCP support is an experimental feature' -- tools only, no resources or prompts. Google also now operates its own public MCP server for its docs (gemini-api-docs-mcp.dev, exposing search_documentation).

skills_concept.notes: CHANGED since 2026-06-21. max_tools_hard.notes: TIER 4 / OBSERVED API ERROR, NOT PUBLISHED SPEC (re-graded 2026-08-19 from tier 2 -- a GitHub issue is tier 4 under methodology section 4 even when it quotes a real API rejection). The cited Gemini CLI issue (opened 2026-02-14, closed 'not planned') reports the verbatim API rejection 'At most 512 function declarations can be specified' when many MCP servers are enabled. UNCONFIRMED BY VENDOR DOCS: on 2026-08-19 I opened the Gemini API function-calling docs (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling -- no numeric cap, only the best practice 'Keep active set to 10-20 tools maximum'), the Interactions API overview (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/interactions-overview), the Live API tools page (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api/tools), the Vertex REST FunctionDeclaration reference and the Gemini Enterprise / Vertex function-calling reference; none of them publishes a maximum number of function declarations. The only tier-1 count Google publishes sits on a DIFFERENT surface: Firebase AI Logic states 'The maximum number of function declarations that you can provide with the request is 128' (https://firebase.google.com/docs/ai-logic/function-calling), presented there as a Firebase AI Logic SDK constraint. Planning guidance: 128 is the conservative documented number on that SDK; 512 is the observed hard rejection point on the raw API. SCOPE: aggregate -- summed across every connected MCP server plus built-in tools in one request; there is no per-MCP-server cap.

max_tools_practical.notes: Google's own function-calling best practices state: 'Tool Selection: Keep active set to 10-20 tools maximum.' Recorded at the top of that band (20). This is vendor ADVICE, not an enforced cap and not a measured cliff, hence medium confidence. Searched for Gemini-specific empirical tool-count degradation data and found none: the most recent public study (Superhuman, June 2026, 584-tool / 110-agent catalog, flat-routing F1 58.2% at 51 tools falling to 42.1% at 584) tested GPT-5.4, GPT-5.1 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 only -- no Google models. The limits that DO bind for Gemini: this ~10-20 advisory band, the 512 aggregate declaration ceiling (an observed API rejection, tier 4 -- see max_tools_hard), and the 1,048,576-token input window.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No deferred/lazy tool loading at the model-API layer -- there is no Gemini analogue of Anthropic's tool-search / defer_loading. Two partial mitigations exist and are NOT the same thing: (a) the Interactions API mcp_server tool takes an allowed_tools allowlist, a static pre-filter applied before definitions reach the model; (b) implicit/explicit context caching amortizes a static tool block. Gemini CLI's Agent Skills do use progressive disclosure, but that defers SKILL.md bodies, not tool definitions.

max_tool_name_len.notes: RE-SOURCED 2026-08-19 to Google's own FunctionDeclaration reference (the previous citation was an unrelated third-party repo issue, tier 4). Firebase's FunctionDeclaration reference states verbatim: 'The name of the function to call. Must start with a letter or an underscore. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores and dashes, with a max length of 64.' Google's Vertex AI REST FunctionDeclaration reference carries the same constraint with dots also allowed: 'Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores, dots and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.' SCOPE: per-tool, API-enforced. This bites MCP servers because hosts namespace tool names -- Gemini CLI prefixes every MCP tool as mcp_{serverName}_{toolName} and truncates names over 63 characters, so a long server name silently eats the 64-character budget.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No documented character or token cap on function/tool description strings; re-checked 2026-08-19 against the function-calling page and the Interactions API reference, which document description as an untyped optional string. The effective constraints are the 1,048,576-token input window and the undocumented 'very large or deeply nested schemas' rejection.

max_request_size.notes: Verbatim: inline data '100 MB per request or payload' with '50 MB for PDFs'; external/signed URLs '100 MB per request/payload'. Larger payloads go through the Files API ('2 GB per file, up to 20GB per project', retained '48 Hours'). This is the HTTP payload ceiling; for text + tool-definition traffic the 1,048,576-token input limit binds first.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented per-functionResponse size cap in bytes or tokens. Gemini 3 models accept multimodal function responses (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, application/pdf, text/plain inline in the response part) and require each response to carry a matching call_id and name. Tool results consume the same 1,048,576-token input budget as everything else.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel function calling is supported with no documented numeric cap on how many calls may be emitted in one turn. Gemini 3 returns a unique id per function call and requires exactly one response per call, matched by id and name -- results may return out of order but must be 1:1.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.unit: automatic function-calling remote calls per request (SDK default)
tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: CHANGED from null. SCOPE: SDK layer, not the model API. The google-genai SDK's automatic function calling loops with a default maximum of 10 remote calls per request; it is configurable and can be disabled, after which the caller drives the loop. The Gemini API itself documents no per-turn numeric cap on tool-call/result cycles -- there is no 'reached its tool-use limit' error analogous to Claude's, so the limits that actually bind a long agentic run are the 512-declaration aggregate ceiling (an observed API rejection, tier 4 -- see max_tools_hard) and the 1,048,576-token input window. The Interactions API does not support Python automatic function calling at all. Source re-pointed 2026-08-19 from the googleapis/python-genai GitHub repo to Google's published SDK documentation site, which states verbatim: 'by default the SDK will perform automatic function calling until the remote calls exceed the maximum remote call for automatic function calling (default to 10 times)'.

Client layer for contrast: Gemini CLI users report tools being 'silently dropped' past roughly 100 aggregate MCP tools (https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21823, closed), and Gemini CLI's docs set a 600,000 ms (10 minute) default per-server request timeout.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Only a subset of the OpenAPI schema is accepted for function parameters (verbatim: 'Only a subset of the OpenAPI schema is supported'). Gemini 3-series and 2.5-series models accept type, nullable, required, format, description, properties, items, enum, anyOf, $ref, minItems, maxItems, minimum, maximum. Documented soft constraint, verbatim: 'For any mode, the API may reject very large or deeply nested schemas' -- Google publishes no numeric nesting-depth or property-count cap, so there is nothing analogous to OpenAI strict mode's 100-property / 5-level rules. Function names are validated by the API against 'Must start with a letter or an underscore. Must be alphanumeric (a-z, A-Z, 0-9), underscores (_), dots (.), colons (:), or dashes (-), with a maximum length of 64.' For MCP the function-calling page adds: 'MCP server names should not include the - character. Use snake_case server names instead.' Sources: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling , https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode/issues/235
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: RATE LIMITS: Google no longer publishes per-model RPM/TPM/RPD tables -- the rate-limits page now says limits 'can be viewed in Google AI Studio' (only Batch API enqueued-token quotas remain tabulated), so the per-model rate numbers carried in the 2026-06-21 revision of this dataset are no longer sourceable and have been removed rather than restated. API CHANGES since 2026-06-21: the Interactions API went GA in June 2026 and is now the recommended surface for all new projects; the sampling parameters temperature / top_p / top_k were deprecated 2026-07-21; thinking_budget is replaced by thinking_level. The Interactions API does NOT support explicit context caching (implicit only, via previous_interaction_id), the Batch API, or Python automatic function calling. Tool configuration is interaction-scoped and must be re-sent on every interaction, so tool-definition tokens are re-paid per interaction unless implicit caching hits. Token accounting now exposes total_tool_use_tokens, total_thought_tokens and total_cached_tokens in the usage payload -- total_tool_use_tokens makes an MCP server's definition footprint directly measurable. MODEL-SPECIFIC: 3.7 Flash is on introductory pricing through 2026-12-31 and doubles on 2027-01-01, so any tool-heavy cost model must carry that step. It is also the default model of the Antigravity managed agent, the only surface with server-side remote MCP today. Minimum cacheable prompt 4,096 tokens.

skills_supported.notes: CHANGED from false. Google now ships Agent Skills: a SKILL.md-based, model-invokable instruction bundle with an official library (github.com/google-gemini/gemini-skills, Apache-2.0), publicised 2026-03-25 and documented on ai.google.dev. IMPORTANT SCOPE: skills live at the AGENT/CLI layer (Gemini CLI, Antigravity, third-party coding assistants), not in the model API -- the Gemini docs state 'Most agents index skills only on startup' and the generateContent / Interactions endpoints neither accept nor process a skill object. For a raw API caller the only always-on instruction channel is still system_instruction, and Gems remain a consumer-product feature.

skills_loading_model.notes: Verbatim (Gemini CLI): 'At the start of a session, Gemini CLI scans the discovery tiers and injects the name and description of all enabled skills into the system prompt' and 'Only skill metadata (name and description) is loaded initially. Detailed instructions and resources are only disclosed when the model explicitly activates the skill, saving context tokens.' Activation is itself a tool call (activate_skill), after which 'The SKILL.md body and folder structure is added to the conversation history'.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Skills never enter a Gemini API request as a first-class object -- the agent host injects skill name+description into the system prompt at session start and appends the SKILL.md body only after activate_skill fires. The resident cost is therefore one metadata line per enabled skill and the burst cost is the skill body, both billed as ordinary input tokens. System instructions are billed as input on every request; caching can absorb a static instruction + tool-definition prefix once it clears the model's minimum cacheable size.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: System instructions are counted as part of the input tokens; Google documents no fixed per-request overhead beyond the caller-supplied content. In the Interactions API tools and system instructions are interaction-scoped and must be re-specified on every interaction, so a large MCP tool block is re-billed each turn unless implicit caching hits.

prompt_caching.notes: Implicit caching is enabled by default for all Gemini 2.5 and newer models; cache hits are reported in usage.total_cached_tokens. Minimum cacheable prompt for Gemini 3.7 / 3.6 / 3.5 Flash: 4,096 tokens (2,048 for Gemini 2.5 Flash and Pro), so a small MCP tool block will not be cached at all. Explicit (manually created) caches work on generateContent but are NOT supported in the Interactions API. Cached read $0.075/1M and storage $0.50/1M/hour through 2026-12-31, then $0.15 and $1.00.

memory_feature.notes: No persistent cross-session memory product in the Gemini Developer API. The closest primitive is the Interactions API's server-side conversation state via previous_interaction_id, which is per-conversation session state (and a caching optimization), not a durable memory store.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Only a subset of the OpenAPI schema is accepted for function parameters (verbatim: 'Only a subset of the OpenAPI schema is supported'). skills_supported.notes: CHANGED from false. skills_loading_model.notes: Verbatim (Gemini CLI): 'At the start of a session, Gemini CLI scans the discovery tiers and injects the name and description of all enabled skills into the system prompt' and 'Only skill metadata (name and description) is loaded initially. Detailed instructions and resources are only disclosed when the model explicitly activates the skill, saving context tokens.' Activation is itself a tool call (activate_skill), after which 'The SKILL.md body and folder structure is added to the conversation history'.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Skills never enter a Gemini API request as a first-class object -- the agent host injects skill name+description into the system prompt at session start and appends the SKILL.md body only after activate_skill fires. The resident cost is therefore one metadata line per enabled skill and the burst cost is the skill body, both billed as ordinary input tokens. System instructions are billed as input on every request; caching can absorb a static instruction + tool-definition prefix once it clears the model's minimum cacheable size.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: System instructions are counted as part of the input tokens; Google documents no fixed per-request overhead beyond the caller-supplied content. In the Interactions API tools and system instructions are interaction-scoped and must be re-specified on every interaction, so a large MCP tool block is re-billed each turn unless implicit caching hits.

prompt_caching.notes: Implicit caching is enabled by default for all Gemini 2.5 and newer models; cache hits are reported in usage.total_cached_tokens. The caching page's minimum-cacheable-prompt table lists Gemini 3.7/3.6/3.5 Flash (4,096) and Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro (2,048) but no Flash-Lite row, so the minimum for this model is undocumented. Explicit caches are not supported in the Interactions API.
